query: For Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain the onset or suppression of corrosion-related degradation in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures? Specify a controlled study that would isolate the governing cause, predicted observations relative to the untreated reference, applicable boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled pre-oxidation treatment that forms a thin, adherent, uniform iron oxide film on the surface of Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state will suppress the corrosion-related degradation when later exposed to harsh environments compared to untreated Q235 steel.
generation.material_initial_state: Q235 steel as received, with its native microstructure and minimal surface oxidation and inherent inclusions characteristic of the alloy.
generation.intervention: Apply a thermal oxidation treatment in air—a controlled heat treatment at a predetermined temperature for a fixed time—to induce the formation of a protective iron oxide (primarily Fe2O3) film on the steel surface prior to environmental exposure.
generation.conditions: After treatment, both the pre-oxidized and the untreated reference samples will be exposed to harsh corrosive conditions at room temperature (e.g., ~20°C) and at an elevated temperature (e.g., ~60°C) in a controlled environment (such as a 3.5% NaCl aerosol or immersion test). Other environmental variables (humidity, oxygen concentration) will be held constant, ensuring that the only variable is the pre-oxidation treatment.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a continuous, adherent iron oxide layer on the steel surface that reduces the rate of electron and ion transfer during corrosion reactions.
generation.mechanism: The passivating oxide film acts as a barrier that limits access of corrosive species (like Cl⁻ and moisture) to the underlying metal, thus reducing the electrochemical reaction sites that drive corrosion under both ambient and elevated thermal conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated Q235 steel, the pre-oxidized samples will show a lower corrosion rate as measured by reduced weight loss and/or lower anodic current densities in electrochemical tests.
generation.baseline: Untreated Q235 steel in its native, pre-exposure state without any pre-oxidation treatment.
generation.boundary: The effect is expected to hold for Q235 steel with its inherent composition and microstructure under the specified test conditions (harsh corrosive environments at room and elevated temperatures) and using the defined pre-oxidation parameters.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the corrosion rate reduction is not precisely predicted and may depend on the exact temperature and duration parameters of the pre-oxidation treatment as well as the severity of the corrosive environment; additional optimization experiments will be required.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of Q235 steel samples: one set receives the controlled thermal pre-oxidation treatment (e.g., heating in air at a controlled temperature and time to develop the oxide film) and the other set remains untreated. Expose both sets to a harsh corrosive environment (such as 3.5% NaCl aerosol or immersion) under two thermal conditions: room temperature (~20°C) and elevated temperature (~60°C).
measurements: Weight loss measurements over a predetermined exposure period
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) to assess corrosion resistance
Surface characterization (e.g., SEM) to observe oxide layer integrity and corrosion morphology
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pre-oxidized samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in corrosion rate (by weight loss or electrochemical parameters) compared to the untreated reference, or if they exhibit accelerated corrosion, then the hypothesis is falsified.
